nodes.summary: The claim of Kourovka Problem 13.28 is false: there are an infinite set $\Omega$ and a subgroup $G$ of the group of permutations of $\Omega$ such that $G$ is cofinitary (every non-identity element of $G$ fixes only finitely many points of $\Omega$) and closed in the topology of pointwise convergence, but $G$ is not locally compact in the subspace topology.
nodes.title: Closed cofinitary permutation groups need not be locally compact

nodes.summary: For every infinite set $\Omega$, every cofinitary subgroup $G$ of the group of permutations of $\Omega$ that is closed in the topology of pointwise convergence is locally compact in the subspace topology.
nodes.title: Claim of Kourovka Problem 13.28

nodes.summary: A subgroup $G$ of the group of permutations of a set $\Omega$ is cofinitary when every non-identity element of $G$ fixes only finitely many points of $\Omega$.
nodes.title: Cofinitary permutation groups
